about: Reviewed exceptions to the derived-content guard (src/dataset/derived-content.test.ts). Each entry names the songs it covers and a ceiling on the note units any one of them may reach in the file, so an exception cannot grow quietly; one that matches nothing fails as stale. See docs/findings/derived-content-inventory.md.

not_derived.reason: Each prompt gives the song's chord symbols. The only pitches are the same two example voicings, repeated in every system prompt.
A model's four-voice voicings of chord symbols. The prompts carried no notes of the songs.
The same voicing task as vl-g8.jsonl, for one song.
Continuations the ceiling model composed in even rhythm at one velocity. Against the real target windows the longest shared pitch run is 2 to 6; nothing is copied from the arrangement.
The script that wrote the composed continuations above.
Per-measure chord voicings the ceiling model wrote. None of the 162 melody measures appears in them.
The annotation names one five-note chord (measure 111) twice. A single sonority, no sequence.
Single anchor pitches and the computed chromatic neighbours around them, from a public-domain work. No arrangement timing or dynamics.
An arpeggio outline of the tonic triad, four pitches, from a public-domain work.
Four opening melody pitches of a public-domain work, pitches only.
Four melody pitches of a public-domain work, quoted as an example of a rejected annotation.

held_for_owner.reason: Amazing Grace vocal route. The GitHub Pages landing page plays site/public/audio/amazing-grace-*.mp3, whose piano bed renders measures 1-10 of the library arrangement (licence unknown) and whose sung line takes its timing from that file. These are the route's inputs. The composition (New Britain, 1829; words 1779) is public domain. Removing them changes a published surface, so the decision is the owner's.
